correctness.rationale: For all fixed N>=2, the first rare arrival is geometric(c/j), common counts conditional on its arrival are multinomial, and their j-scaled deviation from common mean has exact L2 upper bound 1/(c j). This forces a continuous common exponential limit, completion on rare arrival with probability 1-o(1), and a two-point deficit limit. Boundedness justifies first two moments; Popoviciu range bound and c=log(2)/(N-1) give equality in the limiting supremum. Uniform variance tends to zero by almost-sure finite stopping time. Standalone exact rational checker reproduces explicit finite variance fractions and strict difference; no numerical observation replaces the infinite proof.

value.rationale: This solves a natural distribution-free second-moment extremal question for the precise sibling deficit studied in contemporary literature. The exact limit (N-1)^2/4 is attained asymptotically by admissible probabilities, with a mathematically explanatory two-point law; at uniform probabilities variance tends to zero despite maximal mean. The strict rational finite-N counterexample demonstrates why a second-moment result is mathematically different from PGF/binomial-moment order. The result is an exact structural classification for all fixed N rather than an arbitrary isolated slice; it does not claim exact finite-j maximizers or a larger downstream theorem.
